comparison: Perfect match on heterodimer claims (C57-C59, C90). Both evaluations find the evidence supported. OpenEval acknowledges limitations in rigid-body treatment, while peer reviewers highlight the scaffold role of HP1α for HP1β without raising concerns.

Perfect match on integrative model claims (C96-C98). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative language and need for experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing these as valuable testable models for future experiments. Key disagreement on confidence level.

Perfect match on methodology claims (C99-C103). Both evaluations find the methods well-supported. Peer reviewers specifically praise the computational approach as rigorous and well-designed, with clear discussion of assumptions and limits.

Strong overlap on DNA interaction claims (C63-C67, C91-C93). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with cited experimental observations. Peer reviewers highlight DNA's role in tuning phase separation and stabilizing compartments.

Overlap on simulation results for conformational properties (C36-C39). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency and error reporting. Peer reviewers note consistency with previous work and experimental constraints.

Partial overlap on phase coexistence simulation data (C40-C42). Both evaluations find evidence supported. Peer review R1 also includes main conclusions (C2-C3) and literature context (C20-C21), providing broader validation of the overall findings.

Overlap on multicomponent phase behavior (C69-C74). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes phase diagrams and spatial distribution analysis. Peer reviewers highlight spatial separation of paralogs as 'most interesting' example of complex cellular assemblies.

Overlap on scaffold-client mechanism (C86-C89). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval focuses on concentration-dependent partitioning data. Peer reviewers explicitly note HP1α serving as scaffold for HP1β entry into condensed phases.

Overlap on sequential addition experiments (C94-C95). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes differential partitioning behavior. Peer review R5 groups these with broader multicomponent findings (C69-C74) as particularly interesting.

Overlap on domain-swapping experiments for hinge role (C45-C47). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes loss-of-function and gain-of-function phenotypes. Peer reviewers praise the methodical approach and comprehensive insights, highlighting this as innovative.

Overlap on folded domain contributions (C51-C54). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes unexpected CD/NTE cooperation. Peer review R2 also includes hinge and CTE findings (C43-C47), treating domain dissection as comprehensive and innovative.

Partial overlap on contact analysis and mechanistic model (C43-C44). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval focuses on computational evidence for domain interplay. Peer review R2 groups with broader domain-swapping results (C45-C54).

Overlap on mechanistic interpretations (C75-C77). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes synthesis of simulation findings. Peer reviewers note the nuanced interplay between folded and disordered domains elucidating regulatory mechanisms.

Overlap on HP1α-specific phosphorylation site (C78-C79). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes molecular explanation for differential LLPS regulation. Peer review R7 groups with broader mechanistic interpretations (C75-C77, C80-C81).

Overlap on phosphorylation site characterization (C34-C35). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval focuses on regulatory mechanism specificity. Peer review R9 groups with sequence analysis claims (C30-C33) as established characterization.

Overlap on experimental validation of CTE competition (C80). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with simulation findings. Peer review R7 groups with broader mechanistic interpretations (C75-C79, C81).

Overlap on CD contribution and comparison with Swi6 (C83-C84). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval groups C83 with domain-swapping results. Peer reviewers specifically highlight CD contribution as innovative revelation that cannot be overlooked.

Overlap on main conclusions (C2-C3). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive simulation data supporting conclusions. Peer review R1 also includes specific phase coexistence data (C40-C42) and literature context (C20-C21).

Overlap on domain contribution conclusion (C4). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval groups with other main conclusions (C2-C3, C5). Peer review R2 focuses on detailed domain-swapping experiments (C43-C54) that support this conclusion.

Overlap on DNA effects conclusion (C5). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval groups with other main conclusions (C2-C4). Peer review R4 focuses on detailed DNA interaction results (C63-C68, C91-C93) supporting this conclusion.

Overlap on sequence characterization (C30-C33). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval groups with broader structural/sequence characteristics (C1, C6, C10, C23-C29). Peer reviewers treat as established characterization building on experimental results.

Overlap on Swi6 comparison (C84). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate qualification of inference. Peer reviewers highlight CD contribution as innovative finding without challenging the Swi6 distinction.

Minimal overlap on literature context (C20-C21). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval groups extensive literature citations together (C7-C22, C33, C55, C60-C62, C82, C85). Peer review R1 focuses on main findings with brief literature context.

OpenEval R12 addresses extensive literature citations (C7-C22, C33, C55, C60-C62, C82, C85) as established context. No corresponding comprehensive peer review evaluation of literature citations found, though individual claims appear in other peer results.

OpenEval R13 addresses heterodimerization inference (C56) and Swi6 comparison (C84). C84 appears in peer R10, but C56 has no peer review coverage. OpenEval finds both supported based on sequence homology and cited work.

OpenEval R14 addresses experimental validation claim (C80) in isolation. Peer reviewers group C80 with broader mechanistic interpretations in R7 rather than evaluating separately. Both find it supported.

OpenEval R1 comprehensively addresses structural/sequence characteristics (C1, C6, C10, C23-C33). Peer reviewers address subsets (C30-C35 in R9) but no comprehensive peer evaluation of all structural characterization claims found.

Peer R6 addresses conformational characterization (C36-C39) finding evidence supported. OpenEval R3 covers these claims within broader simulation results (C36-C42), also finding them supported with emphasis on error reporting.
